Proposal: dlls/hal/hal.c:151 (compiled only under #if __i386__ || __arm__ || __aarch64__) must not return a made-up 0. Stage 1 needs no privilege: model an absent legacy device as real hardware does, where a read of an unclaimed I/O port floats high (0xFF for a byte, 0xFFFFFFFF for a dword) and a write is dropped, so drivers probing for legacy hardware conclude it is absent. Stage 2 (a decision for the security owner): real port access only through a broker with CAP_SYS_RAWIO and a port allowlist in sg-session, never by giving the unprivileged machine server iopl (CLAUDE.md patch 0005). READ_PORT_ULONG: the 32-bit read of this proposal.

Proposal: dlls/wineps.drv/type1.c:235 get_glyf_pos needs a 'glyf' table; OpenType fonts with CFF outlines have none, so they are not downloaded to the printer. Convert a CFF font to a Type 1 (or CID-keyed Type 0) download: parse the CFF INDEXes, charstrings (Type 2) and subroutines, rewrite each glyph as a Type 1 charstring, and emit the font dictionary; the CFF format and the Type 2 charstring format are Adobe Technical Notes 5176 and 5177 (public PDFs) and the Type 1 format is Adobe's published Type 1 Font Format book. The allowed doc list does not include Adobe documents: the owner must decide whether those public specs may be used. Until then keep falling back to the printer's resident font. Gate: print a CFF OpenType font and check the PostScript output defines the glyphs.
